validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION confirmed independently: EIA Aug2026 Natural Gas Pipeline Projects release (sheet 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects', row 11) carries a matching 'Aspire Energy Express' project (New Pipeline, OH, operator 'Aspire Energy Express LLC', $10M, 300 MMcf/d, in-service 2027); Chesapeake Utilities Corporation's FY2025 Form 10-K (filed 2026, cpk-20251231.htm) and Q2-2026 Form 10-Q (cpk-20260630.htm) both describe, under the heading 'Duncan Plains Pipeline Project', that 'In July 2025, Aspire Energy Express entered into an agreement with American Electric Power to construct and operate an intrastate natural gas pipeline in central Ohio to serve a new fuel-cell facility, which will provide on-site electric power to a data center,' expected in service 1H2027; Chesapeake's PR Newswire release (302499665) corroborates with the AWS/Cologix data-center detail and a ~$10 million capital investment figure. No duplicate: checked against the 46-row roster -- no other row describes this project or corridor. Classification (gas transmission pipeline, not gathering/processing) is correct. NAMING NOTE: SEC filings and the press release never use the sheet's exact pipeline name 'Aspire Energy Express Gas Pipeline' as a project title -- they call it the 'Duncan Plains Pipeline Project' (Duncan Plains is presumably the fuel-cell/data-center site in central Ohio). This is worth recording as an alternate name but is not a naming ERROR: the sheet's PipelineName correctly uses the operating subsidiary's name, which the EIA record also uses ('Aspire Energy Express'). CORPORATE STRUCTURE NOTE: confirmed via the same 10-K/10-Q glossary that 'Aspire Energy Express, LLC' (this project's owner/operator) is legally and organizationally DISTINCT from 'Aspire Energy of Ohio, LLC' (an older gas-distribution subsidiary, ~2,800 mi, 40 OH counties) -- both are wholly-owned subsidiaries of Chesapeake Utilities Corporation (NYSE: CPK), but they are not the same entity and should not be conflated in any GEM row.

validity.recommendation: Treat the sheet's Capacity=300 MMcf/d as medium-confidence only; do not upgrade to high off the AEX company website, which restates an unrelated existing project's capacity, not this project's.
validity.researcher_notes: Capacity=300 MMcf/d is EIA-sourced (Aug2026 release, row 11) and is the only source found that attaches a capacity number to the Aspire Energy Express / Duncan Plains project specifically. However, 300,000 Dth/day (~300 MMcf/d) is ALSO, independently, Chesapeake's stated figure for AEX's EXISTING total firm transportation capacity serving the older, unrelated Guernsey Power Station commitment: (1) aspireenergy-express.com's Gas Projects page states the ORIGINAL Guernsey Power Meter Station project (built 2017-2021, fed from the 42-inch Tallgrass Energy REX pipeline via a relocated 6-inch gathering line) 'provides 300,000 dekatherms/day of natural gas transportation at full pressure, about 1,175 psi'; (2) Chesapeake's FY2025 10-K states 'Aspire Energy Express has been excluded from the table below and had operating revenue of $1.5 million and firm transportation capacity of 300,000 Dts/d for the year ended December 31, 2025' and separately that 'Our transmission business in Ohio, Aspire Energy Express, services one customer, Guernsey Power Station, to which it is the sole supplier' (i.e., as of the FY2025 10-K, the ENTIRE 300,000 Dts/d AEX system capacity is committed to Guernsey; Duncan Plains was not yet in service and carries no capacity figure of its own in either 10-K or 10-Q -- both only give an expected 2027 gross-margin contribution of ~$1.5 million, not a Dth/d design figure). This raises a real possibility that EIA's 'Capacity' field for this 'New Pipeline' project row reused/carried over AEX's existing SYSTEM-level capacity rather than reporting Duncan Plains' actual incremental design capacity, which no primary source states. Not treating this as UNRESOLVED because EIA does affirmatively state the number for this named project row -- but flagging it as a spec concern rather than a clean confirmation, and declining to name a corrected candidate value since no source states the true incremental figure.

Per docs/reference/gem_schema.md, FuelSource must name a specific upstream field/plant/facility feeding the line, never a commodity or a regional shale-play descriptor. No source found names a specific interconnect, field, or upstream facility for the Duncan Plains lateral itself (unlike the older Guernsey Power Station project, whose own page names its upstream tie-in: a relocated gathering line off the 42-inch Tallgrass Energy REX pipeline -- but that is a different AEX project and would be a fabricated attribution if carried over here). The only lead found was Marcellus Drilling News' free-teaser paragraph describing the line as feeding a 'Marcellus/Utica gas' fuel-cell facility -- rejected as a FuelSource candidate on two independent grounds: (1) that detail is absent from Chesapeake's own PR Newswire release, SEC filings, and both company websites (checked directly -- 'Marcellus' and 'Utica' do not appear in any of them), so it is a single, paywalled trade-press mention rather than corroborated fact; (2) even if true, 'Marcellus/Utica' names a shale play/region, not a specific field, plant or facility, so it would not satisfy the column's definition regardless. Leaving blank per the schema guidance rather than defaulting it. [ORCHESTRATOR AUDIT 2026-09-15] Hygiene: tier -> low.
